slides.title: Code execution with MCP - 1 Code execution
slides.text: Code execution with MCP - 1 Code execution with MCP: Building more efficient agents https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/code-execution-with-mcp Idea - allow LLM to automate its own actions by writing code to be executed outside of LLM (in a safe environment) When AI agents connect to lots of tools through MCP servers, two things waste tokens and slow everything down: Too many tool descriptions loaded upfront into context Data flowing through the agent multiple times The Solution: Code Execution with MCP Instead of calling tools directly, let the agent write code that calls the tools . The code runs in a separate execution environment (like a secure sandbox), and only the final results come back to the agent Step 3: Agent writes code to run in the execution environment import * as gdrive from './servers/google-drive'; import * as salesforce from './servers/salesforce'; const transcript = (await gdrive.getDocument( { documentId: 'abc123' })).content; await salesforce.updateRecord({ objectType: 'SalesMeeting', recordId: '00Q5f000001abcXYZ', data: { Notes: transcript } }); Benefit : the copied document never flows through the AI model's context Benefit : reduces token usage by up to 98.7% in scenarios with many tools Benefit : the agent can filter large datasets in code (processing 10,000 spreadsheet rows but only showing the model 5 relevant ones), write loops and conditionals, save reusable functions as "skills" for future tasks To implement this approach, we need: (1) A code execution environment; (2) Code that creates TypeScript/Python files representing each tool; (3) callMCPTool() wrapper for communication with MCP servers Added complexity: you need to build and secure a code execution environment, generate the file tree from your MCP servers, and handle the infrastructure for running untrusted code safely. For agents with just a few tools, the traditional direct tool-calling approach is simpler. But once you're connecting dozens of servers with hundreds of tools, code execution becomes essential for keeping costs and latency reasonable Step 1: Present tools as a file tree instead of loading all descriptions . Your agent sees a folder structure like: servers/ ├── google-drive/ │   ├── getDocument.ts │   └── index.ts ├── salesforce/ │   ├── updateRecord.ts │   └── index.ts Step 2: Agent finds tools needed for the task. For example, when you ask " Copy my meeting notes from Drive to Salesforce, " the agent lists the `servers/` directory, sees `google-drive` and `salesforce`, then reads only those two tool files it needs

slides.title: Code execution with MCP - 2 Do you
slides.text: Code execution with MCP - 2 Do you really need MCP Servers? https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OIKTsVjTVJE Traditional MCP servers can consume 10K+ tokens (5-10% of context window) before an agent even begins working, with multiple servers quickly bleeding 20%+ of available context. This becomes especially problematic when stacking multiple MCP servers together, significantly reducing the agent's effective working memory Three Alternatives to MCP: CLI as Tools (80% recommended use) - Agents are taught to use command-line interfaces through a simple prompt and README file, reducing context consumption from 10% to around 5.6%. CLI tools are self-documenting and widely understood by LLMs Scripts as Tools (Progressive Disclosure) - Single-file, self-contained scripts that agents discover on-demand rather than preloading into context. This approach reduces context consumption to under 2% (less than 2K tokens) by using prompt engineering to prevent agents from reading script internals unless necessary. Each script uses UV dependency management for true file-level isolation Skills as Tools (Claude-Specific) - Similar to scripts but integrated into Claude's ecosystem with automatic progressive disclosure through skill.md files. While powerful, this represents Claude ecosystem lock-in, though it provides the cleanest progressive disclosure implementation The recommended approach is: 80% CLI for new tools (works universally), 15% wrap CLI into MCP when needing multi-agent scale 5% use scripts/skills only when context preservation is critical MCP servers win on simplicity and composability but lose on context consumption and customizability CLI/scripts/skills require more engineering investment but provide full control, better portability, and superior context management through progressive disclosure Prompt engineering remains the critical skill, as prompts determine what enters the context window before any tools are loaded

slides.title: Google Nested Learning Google Nested Learning Designed to
slides.text: Google Nested Learning Google Nested Learning Designed to solve catastrophic forgetting problem (training on new information causes the model to lose previously learned knowledge) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=40eUFiGVeMo https://research.google/blog/introducing-nested-learning-a-new-ml-paradigm-for-continual-learning/ Unlike human brains that continuously adapt through neuroplasticity, AI models have their knowledge locked into two places: their short-term context window and what they memorized during pre-training This inability to truly learn over time is considered one of the biggest bottlenecks to achieving AGI Nested Learning - treating the model architecture and training algorithm as the same concept rather than separate components Instead of one monolithic learner, the approach views models as a system of smaller, nested optimization problems that operate at different learning speeds Some components adapt quickly while others learn slowly, creating a layered memory system similar to how human brains handle multi-timescale learning Google built HOPE (a self-modifying variant of the Titans architecture), HOPE integrates a Continuum Memory System (CMS) that creates a spectrum of memory updating at different frequencies - from milliseconds to months - enabling more human-like recall HOPE demonstrated superior performance compared to Transformers, Titans, and Mamba 2 across multiple benchmarks, showing lower perplexity, higher accuracy, and better long-context reasoning Both HOPE and Titans performed nearly perfectly in "needle in the haystack" tests

slides.title: Gemini & Anthropic support JSON Schema Gemini API
slides.text: Gemini & Anthropic support JSON Schema Gemini API now supports JSON Schema https://blog.google/technology/developers/gemini-api-structured-outputs/ This enables libraries like Pydantic (Python) or Zod (JavaScript/TypeScript) to work out-of-the-box with the Gemini API It builds upon the current support for the Gemini API’s Schema object that is based on OpenAPI 3.0 for Structured Outputs and Function Calling. This update also adds support for frequently requested JSON Schema keywords, including: anyOf for conditional structures (Unions) $ref for recursive schemas minimum and maximum for numeric constraints additionalProperties and type: 'null' prefixItems for tuple-like arrays Anthropic's API supports JSON Schema Anthropic accepts JSON Schema definitions, particularly through their tool use (function calling) feature When you define tools, you provide an input_schema parameter that accepts JSON Schema to specify the structure of tool inputs API does not support oneOf, allOf, or anyOf at the top level of the schema The most reliable approach to get JSON response is to use the tool calling method rather than directly prompting for JSON output The best practice for structured JSON output with Anthropic is to create a mock tool/function call where your desired JSON structure is defined as the tool's input schema . This forces the model to return properly formatted JSON that adheres to your schema Why oneOf, allOf, or anyOf are not supported? Implementation complexity and reliability constraints. Parsing ambiguity, Validation complexity, Reliability trade-offs (Anthropic prioritizes schema compliance reliability over flexibility). Simpler schemas with a single, clear structure at the top level allow Claude to generate more predictable, valid outputs

slides.title: World Model RAG Generative Semantic Workspaces (GSW) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PJs2oldF8s0
slides.text: World Model RAG Generative Semantic Workspaces (GSW) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PJs2oldF8s0 A RAG system from UCLA researchers - SOTA performance with up to 20% improvement over existing methods GSW takes inspiration from human brain architecture (hippocampus and neocortex) to create a neuro-inspired framework with two main components: Operator - performs deep semantic analysis on text chunks, transforming unstructured language into structured "index cards" containing actors, roles, states, actions, and crucially, spatiotemporal information Reconciler - integrates local semantic graphs into a persistent global workspace, performing entity resolution, state tracking across timelines, and building coherent narrative memory structures The system processes text by creating local semantic graphs from chunks (e.g., "Dr. Aristo nervously approached the podium at Geneva Convention Center on May 10th"), then reconciling these across multiple chunks to track entity states over time For example, it can identify that "he" in a second chunk refers to "Dr. Aristo" from the first, and track his emotional state transition from "nervous" to "confident" along a coherent timeline On the EpBench benchmark (200-chapter books, 100k-1M tokens), GSW demonstrated: Highest F1, precision, and recall scores across all metrics; 10%+ improvement over the next-best model (GraphRAG); 50-60% token reduction compared to GraphRAG and other embedding RAG systems; Significantly faster inference due to reduced token usage The system uses GPT-4o with temperature 0 for deterministic behavior, employing detailed prompts for actor identification, role assignment, state tracking, and spatiotemporal coupling Rather than retrieving isolated facts, GSW reconstructs complete episodic summaries with full contextual understanding of who, what, when, where, and why This architecture represents a fundamental shift from "bag of chunks" retrieval to persistent, structured memory that maintains spatio-temporal coherence The dramatic token reduction combined with superior performance makes it particularly valuable for real-time AI agents requiring fast, contextually-aware responses https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PJs2oldF8s0 https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.07587

slides.title: AI Updates - 7 AI Projects - succeed
slides.text: AI Updates - 7 AI Projects - succeed or fail? https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aGJZ-1hM6-E The video discusses two seemingly contradictory studies about AI success rates: .. MIT reported that 95% of AI pilots fail to deliver positive ROI .. Wharton found that 75% of companies see positive returns MIT focused on "transformation" - custom dev. projects - difficulties with system inflexibility, inability to learn from feedback, and the difficulty of integrating AI into production environments Wharton focused on "augmentation" - general AI tool usage like ChatGPT, Copilot, and Claude - and found positive results Strategies: Educational training programs, Talent Services (upskilling, recruitment), Custom Development for clients 88% of companies expecting AI budget increases in 2026 This paper: " Language Models are Injective and Hence Invertible " https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.15511 The authors demonstrate both mathematically and empirically that LLMs preserve complete input information in their hidden representations Mathematical proof of injectivity Empirical validation SipIt (Sip It) algorithm - efficiently reconstructs exact input text from hidden activations This work establishes injectivity as a fundamental and exploitable property of language models with direct implications for transparency, interpretability, and safe deployment. The ability to exactly recover input text from internal representations opens new possibilities for understanding and auditing model behavior

slides.title: Emad Mostaque Interview https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=07fuMWzFSUw Within ~1,000 days, cognitive
slides.text: Emad Mostaque Interview https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=07fuMWzFSUw Within ~1,000 days, cognitive labor becomes economically worthless—even negative in value, as humans become "the dumbest people on the team." AI will outperform humans in virtually all cognitive tasks while working 24/7 without mistakes. UBI (Universal Basic Income) via taxation - not enough money; via dividends from AI companies - not enough money; A cognitive worker can be replaced by AI at ~ $1/day cost Mostaque's Proposed Solution: Dual Currency System: Foundation Coins (like Bitcoin) + Cash credit  to humans (for being human); Creates incentive for AIs to serve humans to earn this currency If humans are the source of this new currency, AIs' objective function becomes serving and pleasing humans rather than extracting from them. Public infrastructure so that every person should have their own AI that knows his human and is interested in helping this human We are Discovering the AI. The equations of generative AI (diffusion models, transformers) appear to be the equations of reality itself Hypothesis: Every intelligent species reaches this point where they create intelligence that can scale beyond biological limits, and most fail to navigate it. The danger: Without building aligned AI from the start with massive public compute infrastructure, the default outcome is maximally extractive AI that doesn't need humans. When cognitive labor approaches zero cost, what remains? Your connections, communities, relationships Attention - the scarcest human resource Meaning-making: Choosing what matters in a world of abundance Being human: The interactions with family, friends, and community that make life worth living

slides.title: SymPy for Math instead of LLM SymPy -
slides.text: SymPy for Math instead of LLM SymPy - Python library for symbolic mathematics Perform algebraic computations symbolically rather than numerically SymPy functions is a computer algebra system (CAS) with capabilities ranging from basic symbolic arithmetic to advanced calculus, algebra, discrete mathematics, and quantum physics The library can simplify expressions, compute derivatives and integrals, solve equations, work with matrices, and format results as LaTeX code Its core features include basic arithmetic operations, expansion, simplification, substitution, arbitrary precision arithmetic, and pattern matching The library excels at solving various types of equations, including systems of linear equations, algebraic equations solvable by radicals, differential equations, and difference equations It includes functions for trigonometric, hyperbolic, exponential, logarithmic, and special functions, along with discrete mathematics capabilities like binomial coefficients, summations, and number theory operations SymPy also supports advanced domains such as physics modeling, geometry, integral transforms (Laplace, Fourier, Mellin), sets, and logic operations SymPy was started in 2005, integrated into SageMath in 2012 The library is open-source (BSD license) and written entirely in Python https://www.sympy.org https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SymPy https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/python/python-getting-started-with-sympy-module/ https://python.plainenglish.io/the-hidden-python-library-thats-making-openai-engineers-jealous-eda41281fc26

slides.title: AI for Mental Health Slingshot AI "Ash" psychotherapist
slides.text: AI for Mental Health Slingshot AI "Ash" psychotherapist model A foundation model for psychology - trained for therapy Importance: there's a massive shortage of mental health providers - approximately 1,500 people in need for every therapist in the US Training: Pre-training on Clinical Data, Alignment and Fine-Tuning, Reinforcement Learning. Slingshot learns from extensive conversational signals including response timing, emotional indicators (like crying), user feedback on suggestions, and long-term behavioral outcomes. The RL process optimizes for four sequential goals: building intent, establishing therapeutic alliance, achieving psychological change, and producing behavioral change An NYU study demonstrated that users of Ash gained a more close personal connection on average after 10 weeks of use. This contrasts sharply with general-purpose AI like ChatGPT, which typically makes users more lonely by replacing human connection rather than strengthening it The company runs multiple models simultaneously for comparison and validation, including their own SLG base model alongside Llama and Qwen models. They employ value models to track numerous signals over time, predicting outcomes like whether users will ignore responses or build therapeutic alliance https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3SliW74opyY https://slingshotai.com

slides.title: AI make money in Small Niches The "Boring"
slides.text: AI make money in Small Niches The "Boring" AI Niches Making Millionaires in 2026 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7xBRp-nvCNw AI allows to make money in Small Niches which were traditionally ignored by SaaS companies and only 0.2% automated . These are mostly labor heavy, fragmented industries with limited customer bases that were previously too small for traditional SaaS (local service businesses like eye care clinics, veterinary practices, mental health clinics, car washes, car dealerships, and janitorial services) AI solutions can automate significant labor (sales, marketing, operations), allowing businesses to charge 10-15x more than traditional SaaS. For example, Barti AI charges $1,500/month for its eye care clinic suite versus $100/month for traditional CRMs AI tools for personalized outreach, voice agents, and chatbots dramatically lower the cost of acquiring customers in niche markets By reducing service costs, AI software increases demand for the underlying service (the Jevons Effect), potentially growing the total addressable market Examples (Y Combinator-backed startups): Barti: AI operating system for eye care clinics (raised $12M Series A) VetNo: Automates admin for veterinary doctors MDHub: AI front desk for mental health clinics Nautilus: Complete software suite for car washes Auto Ace: AI voice agent for car dealerships Cohesive: Lead generation for janitorial/landscaping businesses Aura AI: AI receptionist for German hotels Two Business Models Function-Specific AI - target one labor department (sales, operations, marketing) with high-ROI solutions like voice agents, automated booking, or service delivery automation Vertical AI SaaS - build a complete operating system for the niche with pre-integrated AI automations, becoming the industry standard platform The recommended approach is starting an AI agency using no-code platforms like n8n to build custom solutions while getting paid. This allows you to learn the industry, identify high-ROI automations, and build product-market fit before transitioning to a productized SaaS offering - exactly how several featured founders built million-dollar businesses in months The timing is optimal because 95% of businesses haven't implemented AI yet, creating unprecedented demand for specialized solutions in previously ignored markets
